title: Grading Needs a Rubric, Not Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2608.17938v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Small language models can grade open-ended examination answers as reliably as substantially more expensive models when they grade against an explicit rubric. We test this claim as the design principle behind any-to-bench: a frontier model reads source documents once, at ingestion, to extract each question and its rubric; lower-cost models then perform all repeated grading work. We evaluate six cost-efficient model configurations from two model families at three reasoning-effort levels. Each configuration answers 24 open-ended examination questions, and each also grades every answer sheet three times, yielding 3,456 per-question grades. Scores depend overwhelmingly on the answer being graded: answer identity explains 95.6% of score variance, whereas judge identity explains only 0.2%. translated_title: 评分需要标准，而非智能
translated_abstract: 小型语言模型在依据明确评分标准进行评分时，其可靠性可与成本高得多的模型相媲美，可用于评阅开放式考试答案。我们将这一论断作为“any-to-bench”设计原则的基础：一个前沿模型在摄取源文档时读取一次，提取每个问题及其评分标准；随后，成本较低的模型执行所有重复的评分工作。我们评估了两个模型家族、三种推理努力水平下的六种成本效益模型配置。每种配置回答24个开放式考试问题，并对每份答卷进行三次评分，共产生3，456个逐题评分。得分主要取决于被评分的答案：答案身份解释了95.6%的评分方差，而评判者身份仅解释了0.2%。提高写作者的推理努力水平可使所得分数最多移动满分值的0.143，而提高评判者的推理努力水平则对分配分数的影响微乎其微。
tldr: 本研究证明，使用明确评分标准时，小型语言模型能高效可靠地替代昂贵模型进行开放式答案评分，且评分结果主要由答案本身决定，而非评判者身份。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that small language models can reliably replace expensive models for grading open-ended answers when using explicit rubrics, with scores determined overwhelmingly by the answer itself rather than the judge.
